title: CBI Extension for Edit claim
walkthroughSteps: Apply AC-01: Edit claim details of CLM-2024-008 shows a CBI card under Loss information, read-first.
Press Edit on the card: the same CBI questions as FNOL Loss information. Change something and press Update: the Field / Original / Updated confirm, then a toast.
AC-02 to AC-05 cover the empty, grouped picker, branch-field and add/remove-BI cases. AC-06 is the Claim description label.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC01 · Edit claim details shows the CBI answers read-first
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Edit claim details of CLM-2024-008 (TechStart Pte Ltd, Business Interruption).

**You see:** A card **Contingent business interruption (CBI)** right under Loss information: Caused by CBI Yes, case type Supplier, Named, Supplier name Kestrel Semiconductors Pte Ltd, Supplier industry, Originating loss location. Nothing is an open field until you press **Edit**.

**Try:** Edit, change the supplier name, press **Update (1)**. The confirm table shows CBI third party with its original and updated value. **Confirm changes** gives the toast "Claim details updated". The CBI entities of the open Business Interruption section get the new name too.

Decision: CBI is its own card under Loss information (it refines that card's Type of damage) and above Locations of loss. DESIGN DECISION CBI-EDIT-1 in edit-cbi-card.component.ts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC02 · A Business Interruption claim with no CBI answer asks for it
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Edit claim details of CLM-2024-008 as seeded: Business Interruption, CBI never answered.

**You see:** The CBI card says **Not answered yet** with a short reason and an **Answer** button.

**Try:** Answer, pick Yes, pick a Supplier case type and press Update without a name or location: Update is refused and the missing fields are marked. Fill them in and Update: the confirm table lists every CBI row that changed.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC03 · The 12 CBI case types in one grouped list (open question 2)
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Edit claim details of CLM-2024-008, CBI card in edit mode (press Answer, then Yes).

**You see:** **CBI case type** opens one list with group headings: Supplier, Customer, Denial of Access, Loss of Attraction, Other. Each option keeps its full name so the closed field reads on its own.

**Try:** Apply AC-04b to see a policy that offers only 5 case types: empty groups disappear.

Decision: grouped dropdown, not a radio grid or a two-step picker. One field, the headings do the scanning. DESIGN DECISION CBI-EDIT-2 in shared/utils/cbi-rules.ts. Same list on FNOL Loss information.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC04 · Denial of Access asks whether an authority ordered it
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Edit claim details of CLM-2024-008 with CBI case type Denial of Access, Without PD Trigger (Weather Condition).

**You see:** Read rows include **Access denied by order of an authority: Yes**.

**Try:** Edit and switch to a Supplier type: the authority question goes and the supplier name and location appear. Update: the confirm shows the authority answer being cleared.

Decision: the four Denial of Access types get a required Yes/No "Was access denied by order of an authority?" (the CBI functional-design diagram). Loss of Attraction and (Air)Port Blockage get no extra field: the diagram gives none for Loss of Attraction and leaves Port Blockage open. DESIGN DECISION CBI-EDIT-3.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: AC05 · Adding or removing Business Interruption brings CBI along
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement:
**Opens:** Edit claim details of CLM-2024-001 (Material damage, Financial loss, no CBI).

**You see:** No CBI card.

**Try:** Edit, add **Business interruption** to Type of damage: the CBI card appears already open on the question, since it is now required. Remove Business interruption again: the card goes. On AC-01's claim, removing Business interruption shows the CBI rows being cleared in the confirm table, and the open sections are marked Review needed.

Decision: whether CBI applies and its case type count as section-impacting changes (Review needed); the details (name, industry, location, authority, utility) do not.
